findings.evidence: Filtration.lean:331 `latticeDifferentialWeightDegree_comp_inclusion`; Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/HomologicalComplex.lean:678 `abbrev ofHom {X Y : ChainComplex V α} (f : ∀ i, X.X i ⟶ Y.X i) (comm : ∀ i, f (i+1) ≫ Y.d (i+1) i = X.d (i+1) i ≫ f i)`; grep shows no use of `latticeDifferentialWeightDegree_comp_inclusion` anywhere else.
findings.fix: Add `latticeWeightSublevelComplexInclusion P k hNM : P.latticeWeightSublevelComplex k N ⟶ P.latticeWeightSublevelComplex k M` via `ChainComplex.ofHom`, discharging `comm` with `latticeDifferentialWeightDegree_comp_inclusion`, plus a `@[simp]` lemma for its `.f q` component.
findings.issue: The docstring claims "The inclusions for `N ≤ M` make these complexes the filtered system", but no morphism `latticeWeightSublevelComplex P k N ⟶ latticeWeightSublevelComplex P k M` is exposed — only `weightDegreeInclusion` on chain groups. `latticeDifferentialWeightDegree_comp_inclusion` is exactly the `ChainComplex.ofHom` hypothesis and has no other consumer in the repo, and since the body of `latticeWeightSublevelComplex` is unexposed (no `@[expose]`), a downstream user must transport along the `HEq` differential lemma to build the map.

findings.evidence: Filtration.lean:355-370 `HEq ((P.latticeWeightSublevelComplex k N).d (q + 1) q) …` proved by `heq_of_eq (ChainComplex.of_d …)`; Bounded.lean:55 rewrites with `latticeChainComplex_X` but nothing in the repo uses `latticeChainComplex_d`.
findings.fix: State the usable form: `(P.latticeWeightSublevelComplex k N).d (q+1) q = eqToHom (latticeWeightSublevelComplex_X … (q+1)) ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (P.latticeDifferentialWeightDegree k N q) ≫ eqToHom (latticeWeightSublevelComplex_X … q).symm` and put `@[simp]` on that; keep the `HEq` version unannotated or drop it.
findings.issue: `latticeWeightSublevelComplex_d` is `@[simp]` on an `HEq` between two types that are only propositionally equal (via `latticeWeightSublevelComplex_X`). simp cannot rewrite with such an `HEq`, so the annotation registers only the proposition itself and the differential has no usable characterization; the identical pre-existing `latticeChainComplex_d` is used nowhere, while the `Eq`-shaped `latticeChainComplex_X` is (Bounded.lean:55).

summary: The submodule-level API (mem/single/mono/exhaustion/fg) is complete and correctly annotated, but the complex-level surface stops one step short: the level inclusions are exposed only as degreewise linear maps, and the only characterization of the complex's differential is an inert `@[simp] HEq`, so `latticeWeightSublevelComplex` is effectively opaque to consumers.
